subject: DPA: PII classification, subprocessors & dataflow evidence
messages:
From: Emma Clark <emma.clark@hearthline.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: DPA: PII classification, subprocessors & dataflow evidence

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking this — Hearthline is starting the DPA review and we have a few targeted asks before we can loop in procurement:

1) Full subprocessor roster (names, country, purpose) and whether any have access to plaintext PII.
2) A simple dataflow diagram that shows where PII enters Redwood, how it moves through inference (proxy/LLM), and what is stored (logs, telemetry).
3) KMS custody model (who has key access) and whether keys ever leave customer region.
4) Examples of role-based access controls (screenshots or an export) + audit log retention.

I've attached our initial SSQ so you can see the asks in context (Hearthline_SSQ.xlsx). We're targeting a procurement decision in two weeks, so any evidence we can share ASAP will help.

Can we get a short call tomorrow to walk through the diagram?

Thanks,
Emma Clark
Senior Counsel, Hearthline
emma.clark@hearthline.com

Attachment: Hearthline_SSQ.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Clark <emma.clark@hearthline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: PII classification, subprocessors & dataflow evidence

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline and next steps below.

On subprocessors:
- We'll provide the complete roster and a short purpose map by EOD tomorrow. Names + location + purpose will be included and we'll mark any that may process plaintext PII (most are telemetry, storage, or infra partners).

Dataflow diagram:
- Attached is a lightweight diagram (redwood_dataflow_v1.drawio.png) that shows ingress (API/ingest), proxy/llm serving, KV cache, telemetry pipeline, and long-term logs. It highlights where PII may be transient vs persisted.

KMS custody:
- Our default hosted mode uses customer-managed keys (KMS) in the customer's cloud region for encryption-at-rest of exported artifacts; for hosted customers we offer our KMS-proxy flow (keys stored in HSM-backed KMS; Redwood never retains plaintext keys). We'll provide a short KMS statement and custody diagram.

Access controls & audit logs:
- We can export a sanitized access matrix and sample audit logs (redacted). I will ask Security to prepare a CSV export and a few SSO/SAML screenshots.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Tomorrow 10:00am PT: 30-min call to walk the diagram (I can present).
- EOD tomorrow: subprocessor roster + KMS statement + access_matrix export (sanitized).
- If that looks good, we can send a proposed DPA annex with the residency & subproc clauses for Hearthline legal to review.

If you want a DocuSign-ready DPA annex earlier we can prepare a draft while the evidence is compiled.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachment: redwood_dataflow_v1.drawio.png (diagram image)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: PII classification, subprocessors & dataflow evidence

Rafael / Jonas — quick internal notes before the call:

- Diagram: good start. Add an explicit box for the "KV cache" and mark TTL semantics (how long cached prompt context is kept). Hearthline will care about transient cache retention and replay risk.

- Subprocessors: we should flag any analytics vendors that receive telemetry in US/EU and annotate whether they receive hashed vs plaintext identifiers. Avoid naming until legal approves the wording, but prepare a redline-able annex that includes an optional onshore carve-out if they require EU-only subprocessors.

- KMS: confirm whether the customer's KMS option includes Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) + HSM-backed rotation. If BYOK is available, include steps for key escrow / emergency rotation. If not, we need to call out the proxy model and the associated proof (KMS rotation logs).

- Evidence: I can sanitize an access matrix (remove user ids, leave roles + last-active timestamps). We'll attach as access_matrix.csv and include a link to the audit-log sample.

I'll join the call tomorrow. Rafael — please add Sean (ops) if we need help with the sanitized export.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Emma Clark <emma.clark@hearthline.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA: PII classification, subprocessors & dataflow evidence

Following up from the 10:00am call — notes and artifacts we agreed to share: 

1) access_matrix.csv (attached): role-based mapping + least-privilege justification. This is a sanitized export: user identifiers removed, roles preserved.
2) Sample audit log bundle (link): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/teams/privacy/hearthline-2027
3) KMS statement + custody flow (short doc in drive) — confirms BYOK/HSM options and that keys do not leave customer region for the BYOK model.
4) Updated diagram (we changed TTLs on cache to 1 hour; noted persistence for long-term analytics).

Operational asks for Hearthline legal:
- Please confirm whether they require the onshore-subprocessor carve-out (EU-only) or if the standard roster with notice is acceptable.
- If they want sample audit logs with original timestamps, we'll provide them under an NDA-addendum to limit distribution.

I'll reach out to Ops to prepare the sanitized log bundle and to Legal to draft the annex redlines. Rafael — I added Sean on the CC to help deliver the exports.

Jonas Weber
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Attachment: access_matrix.csv (CSV)
